comment: Shared-Redis-locker variant of pgsl-server.json: identical (PGSL storage backend over
managed Postgres, allow-all, single-root, websockets) EXCEPT the process-local memory
resource-locker is replaced by a SHARED Redis locker. Run it at ONE replica.
THIS IS NOT YET A MULTI-REPLICA CONFIG, and the sentence that used to stand here saying
it was SAFE was a non-sequitur. Moving off the incoherent AzureFile SMB volume onto the
COHERENT Postgres-backed PGSL lattice removed the STORAGE failure that sank the earlier
redis-locker attempt, but storage coherence is NECESSARY, not SUFFICIENT: removing one
failure mode did not establish that no other exists, and one does, a layer up.
The concrete blocker: RedisLocker.clearLocks() does KEYS <prefix>* + DEL across the
WHOLE namespace, and is invoked from initialize() and finalize() -- wired below as
CleanupInitializer / CleanupFinalizer -- while namespacePrefix defaults to the empty
string because this file passes no redisSettings. So replica B booting DELETES every
lock replica A is holding, and A shutting down deletes B's. Scale-up, scale-down and
rolling redeploy are exactly the events that trigger it, and two replicas then interleave
a container read-modify-write and lose a child entry -- the same observable corruption
class as the original torture-test failure, reached by a completely different route.
Enabling >1 replica needs a per-replica namespacePrefix plus an owner-scoped clear, or a
locker whose cleanup is not global.
redisClient is sed-substituted from __REDIS_ADDR__ at boot by docker-entrypoint.sh
(a redis:// URL; locks are ephemeral, Lua-scripted, atomic across replicas).

@graph.comment: Same DataAccessorBasedStore as the file backend, but with the PGSL accessor.
The PGSL-backed DataAccessor. connectionString omitted -> read from PGSL_PG_CONNSTR.
Shared Redis read-write/resource locker across replicas (ephemeral, atomic).
Start the RedisLocker (and clear any stale locks) on boot.
Close the Redis connection + delete remaining locks on shutdown.
